findings.finding: The sentinel/cache recipe in the test obligation is under-determined and, executed in the written order, cannot install the sentinel at all. It says to 'clear both module cache entries, replace the shared Existing export by a unique object sentinel, reload Screen'. Once the require.cache entry for src/shared/ui/Existing.js is deleted there is no loaded module object left whose export can be replaced; and if the implementer re-requires it first, that fresh load re-reads module.exports = {Existing: true} from disk and discards any sentinel installed beforehand. The ordering is load-bearing rather than incidental, because Screen captures the binding by destructuring at require time, so the sentinel must be installed after Existing is loaded and before Screen is reloaded, and Existing's cache entry must not be cleared again in between. As written, two implementers can both 'comply' while one produces a test that never exercises the identity property.
evidence: TEST-d1031be79ec889e437494667.expected: 'In another isolated child Node process verify the normal Existing value, clear both module cache entries, replace the shared Existing export by a unique object sentinel, reload Screen and assert reference identity. Restore caches in finally.'

src/features/example/Screen.js@abde643 read as 'const {Existing}=require("../../shared/ui/Existing");module.exports={Existing};' — the value is captured by destructuring at load time, not read through a live getter
src/shared/ui/Existing.js@abde643 read as 'module.exports = {Existing: true};' — a re-require after cache deletion reconstructs this object from disk, overwriting any previously installed sentinel
findings.required_correction: Replace the recipe with the exact ordered steps: require Screen and Existing and assert the normal value; delete only the require.cache entry for src/features/example/Screen.js; require src/shared/ui/Existing.js and set its Existing export to a unique object sentinel; require Screen again and assert Screen.Existing === sentinel by reference; in finally restore the original Existing export value and delete both cache entries so no mutated module leaks. State explicitly that the Existing cache entry must not be cleared between sentinel installation and the Screen reload.

findings.finding: The criterion records component_decision CREATE for a change whose impact is MODIFY of an already existing GIT_TREE module, and its reuse search omits the host module itself. The reuse search lists only src/shared/ui/Existing.js, so the file actually being changed — which already exists and already carries the re-export the constraints require preserved — was never considered as a reuse or extension target. This passes mechanically (normalizeReuse only forbids a selected_component_candidate_id under CREATE and never cross-checks the decision against the impact change_kind), but it reads as a greenfield creation and invites an implementer to rewrite Screen.js wholesale and drop the Existing import, which is precisely the preservation property this slice depends on.
evidence: CRT-51417fd314d2e6f58419be14.decision_justification: 'Create the disposable functional module in the declared application path' — describes creation of a module that already exists

IMP-fadee6dec904187464cebf95: change_kind 'MODIFY' on CAND-c9a359f109c1971df53023bc (src/features/example/Screen.js), candidate_origin GIT_TREE; the file exists at abde643 and already re-exports Existing

findings.required_correction: Either set component_decision to EXTEND with selected_component pointing at src/features/example/Screen.js and add CAND-c9a359f109c1971df53023bc to reuse_search_candidate_ids, or keep CREATE and amend decision_justification to state explicitly that CREATE scopes only the new toggle symbol added inside an existing module whose Existing import and re-export must survive unchanged.

findings.finding: The preserved shared-export identity has no independently observed proof. The plan constrains Screen.js to keep an Existing re-export identical to the shared module export, but the only independent (non-delivered-test) observation declared is the toggle transition pair. Byte-for-byte hashing covers src/shared/ui/Existing.js, which is unchanged and therefore cannot witness anything about the re-export inside the file that does change. That leaves the identity property resting entirely on the delivered test's exit status, which the plan elsewhere insists must not be consumed as a success flag. An exit status of 0 cannot distinguish 'identity asserted and held' from 'identity assertion never executed' — and the obligation's own 'Restore caches in finally' construct is a classic way for a throw to be masked or for the assertion to be skipped silently.
evidence: PLAN-f0ffd6b4bf9fa1a751454c58.implementation_constraints: 'Keep the Existing import and re-export in src/features/example/Screen.js identical to the export from src/shared/ui/Existing.js.'

findings.required_correction: Close the gap one of two ways, and bind it to IMP-fadee6dec904187464cebf95: either (a) extend the independent isolated observer so that, in the same fresh process and after the toggle pair, it evaluates reference identity between the Existing value exported by src/features/example/Screen.js and the one exported by src/shared/ui/Existing.js and records it as an observed proof_result; or (b) require the delivered test receipt to enumerate per-assertion executed/outcome entries rather than a single exit status, so a skipped identity assertion is distinguishable from a passing one.

findings.finding: The proof obligation does not pin how the two documentary scenarios are bound to observations. Its expected text says scenario proof_results come from 'independent isolated Node transition calls' (plural, unscoped), while the plan item constrains orchestration to 'independently call toggle twice in a fresh Node process' (one process). Under the per-scenario reading, toggle-on-off can never be observed from its declared given state ('Selection is on'), because a fresh process re-enters the initial 'off' state defined by the requirement. Worse than a false FAIL, this permits a false PASS: an observer restarting per scenario records true for both calls and can mark toggle-on-off satisfied using an observation that is actually the off->on transition. Nothing in the proof text forbids that binding.
